Hi Sofia — great to meet earlier. Looping in Laura (procurement/tax owner) and Ben (vendor tax) to confirm the exact checklist and timeline.

At a high level, to activate a vendor and start issuing POs from Redwood's procurement system we typically need:
- Completed vendor onboarding form (PDF) with legal entity and bank wiring details
- VAT registration certificate (PDF) if the vendor is VAT-registered in the supplier country
- Proof of bank account ownership (bank letter or voided bank statement)
- Local tax residency or fiscal representative letter if requested by local law (rare, but sometimes required for certain EU markets)
- Point of contact for billing and who will receive POs / invoices

On withholding / reverse charge: Redwood applies local tax policy by country. For EU suppliers with a valid VAT registration we usually process invoices under reverse charge (no withholding) provided the VAT number validates and the invoice contains the required reverse-charge language. Ben, Laura — can you confirm any Redwood-specific wording we need on the final invoice and whether we need a Supplier Self-Cert form for Irish vendors?

Sofia — I'll keep you posted on the exact PDF to complete; for speed, if you can share the VAT cert and bank letter we'll start the internal validation.

Best,

Alex / Ben — quick procurement checklist and Redwood requirements for EU (Ireland) non-US vendors. Putting this here so Sofia has a single action list.

Required for PO enablement (must be PDF and legible):
- Vendor onboarding form (our standard) — fields: legal name, registered address, VAT/Tax ID, payment currency, bank IBAN + BIC, remittance email, billing contact. (I've uploaded the current template to Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1abcOnboardingForm).
- VAT registration certificate (issued by Irish Revenue) — we validate number format and run an invoice sample check.
- Bank letter of authority confirming IBAN/Beneficiary — required for vendor payment mapping.

Tax-specific notes for Ireland / reverse charge:
- If the vendor supplies services and provides a valid Irish VAT number, Redwood will accept reverse-charge treatment (no Irish VAT charged) as long as the supplier's VAT number validates in VIES and the invoice states "reverse charge applies".
- Redwood does not withhold Irish corporate tax in these cases. Withholding is only applicable where local law or treaty requires it (rare for EU services).
- For certain PASSTHROUGH goods or when vendor requests to be taxed in their local jurisdiction, we may request additional documentation (fiscal rep letter).

Timing: once we receive: (1) completed onboarding form, (2) VAT cert, and (3) bank letter, procurement can create the vendor record and enable PO issuance within 2 business days (barring missing fields).

Action items for Ares Global (Sofia):
- Fill and return the vendor onboarding PDF (signed)
- Attach VAT registration cert (PDF) and bank letter of authority
- Confirm remittance email and invoice recipient

Ben — can you confirm whether we need the Supplier Self-Cert for Irish vendors or any additional tax attestation?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Procurement Manager
